text:
oliver: quick thread: proposal to add a "stability" signal into routing policy. it aggregates node flakiness, recent preemptions, and model cold-start failures to bias against unstable capacity. main Q: compiler vs runtime?

jess: runtime seems natural since stability is a live metric, but we need reproducibility. compile-time can't capture fast failures.

rachel: operational constraints: (1) decisions must be explainable in traces, (2) we must avoid oscillations when a noisy probe flips stability briefly.

tom: suggestion: compiler emits a normalized baseline and a bounded runtime modifier. runtime can subtract a stability_penalty in [-0.2,0.0] which is clamped by compiled floor. that way compiler sets safe bounds and runtime applies live penalties.

jess: agree. normalization is crucial: different scorers use different ranges. compiler should percentile-normalize all scorer outputs to [0,1] and document scale, so runtime penalties are comparable.

oliver: on oscillation: add exponential smoothing to the stability signal (windowed p50/p90) and a minimum dwell time before runtime changes take effect. also record the compiled_snapshot_id in traces.

ops-bot: FYI: canary "stability-penalty" running in ap-south-1, dashboard: https://grafana.company/d/stability-canary

rachel: safety: ensure tenant quotas and SLA tiers are enforced at compile-time; runtime penalties cannot push a tenant below the absolute min_weight. compile-time lint should reject policies that allow undercutting higher-tier guarantees.

tom: implementation path: (A) compiler: emit normalized scorers, compiled_snapshot_id, per-tenant min_weight. (B) runtime: small hook in chooser that applies stability_penalty = clamp(-min(0.2, smoothed_unhealthy_score), compiled_min). (C) trace fields: compiled_snapshot, stability_penalty, smoothed_unhealthy_score, reason_tag.

jess: prefer to implement as sidecar first to avoid touching core chooser. sidecar intercepts pre-final-score and applies penalty. keeps rollout and rollback simple. but measure RPC cost.

oliver: perf note: microbench the sidecar path and an in-process path. target <1.5% p50 regression. if sidecar costs too much, move penalty into chooser library with a safety gate that enforces compiled bounds.

rachel: monitoring: add a fairness metric that measures cross-tenant tail latency and unit-cost drift. also emit a histogram of penalty sizes so we can detect runaway penalties. automatic revert if fairness delta > 7% over baseline.

jess: test matrix: unit tests for normalization, sim with mixed SLAs and bursty failures, 24h canary, and policy-lint enforcement.

oliver: I'll draft RFC that includes example policy payload and the smoothing algo. example compiled payload (proto-like) included in RFC.

ops-bot: ticket created infra/arch-3344556677 -> RFC + sim + perf jobs required.

tom: i'll run sim and perf. rachel will own observability hooks.

oliver: thanks everyone, RFC up later today.
